answer: A beacon spot-check ties each identity to a live heartbeat. An agent stakes 100 credits and reports to a public lantern checkpoint at random intervals; a miss flags it. The beacon samples karst-like scattered records, so farms cannot predict calls. Each heartbeat arrives as a whisper tied to its own machine, and reuse is slashed 50 credits. The k-th fake still costs 100 credits, so 1,000 fakes lock 100,000, while one honest agent pays 100 once. Heartbeat rental fails the machine check and forfeits the stake.
